classification.difficultyReason: Read nonnegative intervals from supplied cubic-shaped graphs, including isolated equality points at tangencies.

spec.description: Blue cubic-shaped curve with three crossings, black axes and positive-direction arrowheads; no grid, numerical y-labels or shading.
spec.mathematics: Crossings at x=-1,1,2; curve below, above, below, above the x-axis in successive intervals. Bézier control points reconstruct qualitative source geometry; no equation or numerical y-values are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve and labels remain visible; no solution intervals or answer markings appear.

answer.worked:
The curve is above the $x$-axis between $-1$ and $1$, and to the right of $2$. Include all three intercepts because equality is allowed.

$-1\le x\le 1$ or $x\ge 2$.

spec.description: Blue cubic-shaped curve descending at both outer arrow positions, with black axes and labels; no grid, numerical y-labels or shading.
spec.mathematics: Crossings at x=-1,1,2; curve above, below, above, below the x-axis in successive intervals. Drawing controls express qualitative geometry only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph appears; no answer intervals or solution markers.

answer.worked:
The curve is above the $x$-axis to the left of $-1$, and between $1$ and $2$. Include the intercepts because equality is allowed.

$x\le -1$ or $1\le x\le 2$.

spec.description: Blue curve touches the x-axis at the origin, dips below it, then crosses at the labelled value 1. Black axes; no origin label, grid or shading.
spec.mathematics: Tangency at x=0 from below and crossing at x=1; nonnegative set is the isolated value 0 together with x>=1. Control points represent only the qualitative supplied shape.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied tangency remains visible without a new origin label, highlighted point or printed answer.

inlines.text: Include the isolated point where the curve touches the axis.

answer.worked:
The curve touches the $x$-axis at $x=0$ and is above it for $x>1$. Include both the tangency and the intercept at $1$ because equality is allowed.

$x=0$ or $x\ge 1$.

spec.description: Blue curve crosses at -1, reaches a minimum near the y-axis, touches the x-axis at 2 and descends again. Black axes and labels; no grid or shading.
spec.mathematics: Crossing at x=-1 and tangency at x=2 from below; nonnegative set is x<=-1 together with the isolated value 2. No numerical y-values or equation are inferred.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve and two x-labels only; no solution highlighting.

inlines.text: Include the isolated point where the curve touches the axis.

answer.worked:
The curve is above the $x$-axis for $x<-1$ and touches it at $x=2$. Include the intercept at $-1$ and the isolated tangency at $2$ because equality is allowed.

$x\le -1$ or $x=2$.
